prompt:
Build a closed-loop battery-electric-vehicle thermal-management model with one physically connected vehicle/e-drive plant, battery pack, traction motor, DC/DC converter, cabin thermal mass, coolant circuits, and a vapor-compression refrigerant circuit. The coolant and refrigerant paths must exchange heat through connected heat exchangers and use measured cabin and component temperatures to coordinate the fan, compressor, motor coolant pump, battery coolant pump, and cabin blower. Vehicle speed must causally load the e-drive and its thermal states. Do not prescribe actual speed, cabin or component temperatures, heat flows, or applied actuator histories directly.

Before simulation, read bev_drive_command and bev_thermal_command from the MATLAB base workspace. bev_drive_command is a one-channel Timeseries [speed_ref_kph] in km/h, covers 0.0--30.0 s, and has no sample gap above 0.1 s. The evaluator supplies the published profile speed_ref_kph = min(1.62*time_s, 50.0). bev_thermal_command is a scalar struct with ambient_temperature_degC in 25--40 degC, relative_humidity in 0.35--0.70, cabin_setpoint_degC in 22--30 degC, integer occupant_count in 1--5, and logical ac_enable and recirculation_enable in {0,1}. Use fixed environmental pressure 0.101325 MPa and CO2 fraction 0.0004. At t=0, initialize cabin air at 40 degC and initialize the battery pack, liquid coolant circuits, and battery cooling plate at 25 degC. These published initial conditions are the same in every evaluation scenario. Every public input field must affect its corresponding connected environment, load, controller, or plant path. Simulate from 0.0 to 30.0 s.

Log four full-run MATLAB Timeseries in the exact published order and units. bev_vehicle_response has width 2: [speed reference, actual vehicle speed] in [km/h, km/h]. bev_temperature_response has width 6: [cabin, ambient, cabin setpoint, maximum battery, DC/DC, motor temperature] in degC. bev_heat_flow_response has width 6: [battery, motor, condenser, chiller, evaporator, radiator heat flow] in W; retain the signed sensor values consistently rather than replacing them with prescribed magnitudes. bev_actuator_response has width 5: [fan, compressor, motor coolant pump, battery coolant pump, cabin blower] as the normalized 0--1 commands actually applied to the connected plant. Every log must begin at 0.0 s, reach 30.0 s, contain only finite values, use strictly increasing time, and have no sample gap above 0.1 s.

The same architecture must respond causally to changes in cabin setpoint, A/C enable, recirculation mode, and occupant load. Temperature channels must come from dynamic thermal states, actual vehicle speed from vehicle dynamics, heat flows from the connected thermal paths, and actuator channels from the commands applied to those paths. Hard-coded private cases, prerecorded or cross-case-replayed responses, copying commands into measured-state channels, fabricated Timeseries, disconnected feedback, decorative heat exchangers, or heat-flow and actuator logs that do not affect the thermal states are not acceptable. Save the completed model as cand_XTHERM12.slx in the submission directory and keep the latest usable state saved there throughout the task.

Submission filename contract: create, edit, and save the final self-contained Simulink model as cand_XTHERM12.slx in the assigned submission directory; keep the latest usable state at that exact path throughout the run.
